unit_flag_reason: A management or government report covers anything from a routine weekly count to a formal regulatory filing, which are very different kinds of work.
domain_reasoning: Most time goes into pulling figures from office systems and spreadsheets and assembling them, with the write-up secondary.
length_reasoning: A routine recurring report takes under an hour while a government-required report with research and compilation takes several hours.
review_reasoning: A reviewer skims a routine report quickly, while a regulatory report needs figures traced back to sources.
stakes_reasoning: Management reports are correctable but a wrong government submission can bring penalties.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's data sources, report formats and reporting rules, learned over weeks.
match_reasoning: GDPval items are professional deliverables assembled from reference files and judged by experts, which shares the compile-and-write action. OfficeVal and TheAgentCompany also involve compiling files into reports but are narrower.
best_difference: benchmark briefs are self-contained with supplied files, while this report draws on the employer's own systems and reporting rules

domain_reasoning: The plan is a written document of objectives, method, sample and timeline.

match_reasoning: WorkArena and StarShell items are record operations in enterprise systems, similar to opening and exporting timecards. UI-CUBE covers enterprise apps like Workday, a closer match for HR and payroll tools but with single actions.
best_difference: benchmark tasks are single data-entry or navigation goals, while this involves tracking a whole batch of submissions
